title: TIDFormer: Exploiting Temporal and Interactive Dynamics Makes A Great Dynamic Graph Transformer

problem.claim: Transformer-based dynamic graph neural networks need to define self-attention mechanisms appropriately and encode temporal and interactive dynamics comprehensively without extra complex modules.

gap.claim: Previous works use uninterpretable self-attention definitions on dynamic graphs, and their effectiveness and efficiency vary significantly.

contributions.claim: TIDFormer is a dynamic graph Transformer designed to exploit temporal and interactive dynamics efficiently.

The method uses calendar-based time partitioning, interaction embeddings from sampled first-order neighbors for bipartite and non-bipartite graphs, and a simple decomposition to jointly model temporal and interactive features.
The work clarifies and verifies the interpretability of its self-attention mechanism for dynamic graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on several dynamic graph datasets.
The authors report that TIDFormer outperforms state-of-the-art models across most datasets and experimental settings.
The authors report significant efficiency advantages over previous Transformer-based methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing dynamic graph neural networks use Transformer architectures to capture sequential graph evolution.
Transformer-based approaches differ substantially in effectiveness and efficiency, motivating clearer self-attention definitions and comprehensive dynamic encoding.
TIDFormer exploits temporal and interactive dynamics through interpretable self-attention, time partitioning, neighbor-based interaction embeddings, and feature decomposition.
Experiments on several dynamic graph datasets are reported to show effectiveness and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The method combines explicit temporal partitioning with interaction embeddings derived from sampled first-order neighbors.

interpretation.claim: Separating temporal structure from local interaction structure may provide a compact way to represent dynamic graphs.

application.claim: For dynamic graph modeling, consider calendar-aware temporal features and sampled-neighborhood interaction representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach works equally well across graph types, datasets, or sampling regimes.

source_observation.claim: The authors report efficiency advantages from jointly modeling temporal and interactive features with a simple decomposition.

interpretation.claim: A simpler decomposition may reduce the cost of combining multiple dynamic signals.

application.claim: When designing dynamic graph models, evaluate simple feature decompositions as alternatives to adding complex modules.

exception.claim: The abstract provides no quantitative efficiency measurements or details about computational tradeoffs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the self-attention formulation or decomposition in sufficient implementation detail.
The abstract does not provide ablations, limitations, or independent verification.
